problems.original_statement: Marginal structural models, the parametric g-formula, g-estimation and longitudinal targeted learning all identify sustained-regime effects under sequential exchangeability and positivity, and all of them require nuisance models for treatment, censoring and outcome. When those nuisance models are fitted by machine learning, the model that predicts treatment best is not the model that produces the best causal estimate: a highly adaptive learner can achieve excellent discrimination while returning near-zero treatment probabilities, poor longitudinal balance and invalid inference. Standard cross-validation selects on prediction loss and is blind to all three. No selection criterion in routine use combines treatment prediction with longitudinal balance, weight dispersion and an estimate of the influence-function remainder, and no default library is tuned for the causal objective rather than the predictive one.
problems.correction_note: Balance-based criteria for the weight model are already in use: calibrated weights fitted with SuperLearner have been implemented and applied to longitudinal cohorts, so the claim that no selection criterion departs from prediction was too strong. The identification requirements also include consistency alongside sequential exchangeability and positivity, and different estimators require different nuisance components, which the entry flattened.
problems.statement: Identifying a sustained-strategy effect requires consistency, sequential exchangeability and positivity, and the estimator families differ in which nuisance components they need. When those components are fitted by machine learning, the model that predicts treatment best is not the model that minimizes the finite-sample error of the causal estimator: a highly adaptive learner can achieve excellent discrimination while returning near-zero treatment probabilities, poor longitudinal balance and invalid inference. Balance-calibrated weight fitting exists and has been applied, so the field is not selecting on prediction alone. What is missing is a criterion that combines predictive risk with the estimator-specific diagnostics that matter, longitudinal balance, weight tails and the remainder-rate condition, in one selection rule, and a default library tuned that way rather than for prediction.
problems.why_open: The causal loss is not computable the way a predictive loss is, because the contrast being targeted is never observed, so the quantity one would cross-validate against does not exist as a label. Balance and weight-dispersion criteria are computable and are not losses in the decision-theoretic sense, and a learner can optimize them while fitting poorly. Which diagnostics apply depends on the estimator, so a single universal criterion is the wrong object and a family of estimator-specific ones has to be built and validated separately.
problems.proposed_direction: Construct selection rules that combine predictive risk with longitudinal standardized differences, weight-tail behavior and an estimate of the influence-function remainder, specified per estimator rather than universally, and test whether they select models with lower causal bias than predictive cross-validation on the same data. Compare weighted marginal structural models, sequentially doubly robust estimators, longitudinal targeted learning and Bayesian g-computation under deliberate misspecification of each nuisance component in turn. Cross-fit at the patient level rather than the record level, and report the empirical standard-error ratio and convergence failures with the bias, since an estimator that fails to converge on a fifth of replicates is not competitive at any bias.

problems.original_statement: Treatments, outcomes and clinical observations occur asynchronously and are recorded at times determined by the care process. Almost every applied g-method assumes a prespecified discrete grid, and discretization can reverse temporal ordering between a treatment and an outcome that fell in the same interval, merge multiple events into one, or define an estimand that exists only relative to the chosen interval. General identification results for dynamic regimes under irregular observation, treatment-dependent visiting and within-interval effects remain limited, so the applied analyst working in continuous time has a modeling apparatus without an identification theorem to sit under it.
problems.correction_note: Continuous-time identification and efficient estimation for dynamic interventions under counting-process filtrations and irregular monitoring have been established, so the claim that the analyst has no identification theorem was wrong. What those results do not yet settle is the treatment-dependent informative visit process together with within-interval effects, as an apparatus an applied analyst can use by default.
problems.statement: Treatments, outcomes and clinical observations occur asynchronously and are recorded at times determined by the care process. Discretizing that onto a grid can reverse the temporal ordering of a treatment and an outcome falling in the same interval, merge several events into one, and define an estimand that exists only relative to the chosen interval. Identification and efficient estimation for dynamic interventions in continuous time under counting-process filtrations and irregular monitoring have been established. They do not yet settle the case an emulation on routine data actually faces: a visit process that depends on treatment, combined with effects that occur inside an interval. A continuous-time emulation must define the treatment, covariate, visit, censoring and outcome processes relative to a filtration and impose assumptions linking latent histories to the observed visit process, and most applied emulations still discretize without an identification result tied to the grid they chose.
problems.why_open: In continuous time the treatment, visit and outcome processes are counting processes whose intensities depend on one another, so sequential exchangeability has to be stated with respect to filtrations rather than a fixed sequence of covariate vectors, and the resulting conditions are stronger and harder to interpret. Grid-refinement analyses can reveal sensitivity to discretization and cannot establish identification, so the diagnostic available to applied work does not answer the question it raises. There is also no natural sample-size asymptotics, because information about an intensity comes from event counts rather than from patients.
problems.proposed_direction: Extend the existing continuous-time identification results to treatment-dependent visiting with within-interval effects, and state which conditions a standard electronic health record violates. Combine marked point-process models, continuous-time structural nested models and neural differential equations, constraining the learned components to the nuisance functions identification actually requires, so flexibility sits where it cannot manufacture a contrast. Report invariance across nested grids as a routine diagnostic while stating what it does and does not establish.

problems.original_statement: A database of millions can carry very little information about a specific target trial once strict eligibility, active-comparator restriction and weighting have been applied, and extreme weights reduce the effective sample size much further than the nominal count suggests. Conventional asymptotic inference then becomes unreliable, most sharply for rare competing events and for subgroup effects, which are precisely the quantities decision-makers ask about. Papers continue to report the nominal number of patients, which for a weighted longitudinal analysis is not the quantity that governs the variance.
problems.correction_note: No auditor found the claim overstated. The statement is retained with the effect of near-positivity on weighted longitudinal survival estimation cited, which supplies the mechanism the entry asserts.
problems.statement: A database of millions can carry very little information about a specific target trial once strict eligibility, active-comparator restriction and weighting have been applied, and extreme weights reduce the effective sample size far below the nominal count. Conventional asymptotic inference then becomes unreliable, most sharply for rare competing events and for subgroup effects, which are the quantities decision makers ask about. Papers continue to report the nominal number of patients, which for a weighted longitudinal analysis is not the quantity that governs the variance, and no convention requires the effective size to appear beside it.

problems.original_statement: The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population and discards information, with an estimand that is often left unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust and computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. A study reporting one of these reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown, and nothing requires that at least one weighting, one outcome-modeling and one doubly robust estimator be compared on the same data.
problems.correction_note: The proposed requirement was too strong. Every emulation need not compare all three estimator families; what a study owes is a justification of its prespecified estimator against the exact estimand, data structure, overlap and nuisance assumptions, with prespecified alternatives targeting the same contrast where that is feasible.
problems.statement: The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population, discards information, and often leaves its estimand unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust, computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. No estimator is defensible as a universal default, and a study reporting one reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown: nothing requires the choice to be justified against the estimand and the data structure, and nothing requires a prespecified alternative targeting the same contrast.
problems.why_open: Comparing estimators multiplies the analysis cost and can produce disagreement the paper then has to explain, which is a strong disincentive. There is no accepted way to report disagreement between estimators targeting one estimand under different nuisance assumptions: it is neither a sensitivity analysis in the usual sense nor a robustness check. Simulation evidence comparing the families is fragmented across papers with different generating mechanisms, so no synthesis exists that would justify a default even if one were wanted.
problems.proposed_direction: Require that the prespecified estimator be justified against the exact estimand, data structure, overlap and nuisance assumptions, and that at least one prespecified alternative targeting the same contrast be reported where feasible, so estimation sensitivity is visible without mandating three families in every study. Build a public benchmark with realistic observation processes and missingness on which the families are compared under a common generating mechanism, turning the fragmented simulation evidence into a synthesis. Score methods on failure awareness as well as bias and coverage: an estimator returning a narrow interval in a deliberately non-identifiable scenario has failed the test that matters most.
